hook: Who are Indians, and where did we come from?
hookSay: Tony Joseph's book, Early Indians, tells the story of our ancestors using ancient {DNA|D N A}. Now you can explore it on a map.

beats.label: 1 · The First Indians
beats.say: Modern humans left Africa and reached India about {65,000|sixty-five thousand} years ago. Their descendants still make up {50|fifty} to {65|sixty-five} percent of our ancestry.

beats.label: 2 · Farmers and cities
beats.say: After {7000|seven thousand} {BCE|B C E}, farmers from Iran's Zagros hills moved east, mixed with the First Indians, and helped build the Harappan civilization.

beats.label: 3 · The Harappans
beats.say: For {700|seven hundred} years, from {2600|twenty-six hundred} to {1900|nineteen hundred} {BCE|B C E}, its cities show no sign of being attacked or burnt.

beats.label: 4 · The last migrants
beats.say: After {2000|two thousand} {BCE|B C E}, herders from the Eurasian Steppe arrived, bringing Indo-European languages.

beats.label: 5 · The Indian pizza
beats.say: The book calls us a pizza: a First Indian base, a sauce of Zagros farmers, a sprinkle of Steppe cheese, and toppings from east Asia.

beats.label: Explore
beats.say: Scrub one long timeline, take a guided map tour, and browse every picture in the book.

outro: No group is pure. We are all migrants. Explore Early Indians, the interactive atlas, at the link below.
